weak_references.ml_adjusted_r2: adjusted R^2 is checked by the same definition rearranged with numpy (residual variance over the sample variance); R^2 by scikit-learn
weak_references.ml_bias_variance_decomposition: checked by a numpy computation of the same definitions; the decomposition identity (expected MSE computed directly equals bias^2 + variance) is an independent check of the two parts
weak_references.ml_davies_bouldin_index: checked by a scipy (cdist) computation of the same definition; scikit-learn's davies_bouldin_score agrees only to about 1e-8 because of its dot-product distance formula
weak_references.ml_focal_loss: the loss value is checked against the torchvision sigmoid_focal_loss formula re-implemented in PyTorch (an independent implementation of the same definition); the gradient by PyTorch autograd
weak_references.ml_gini_split: checked by a different computation of the same impurity (the probability that two draws with replacement differ), in numpy
weak_references.ml_hinge_loss: the squared hinge loss is checked by a numpy re-derivation of the same definition; the hinge loss by scikit-learn
weak_references.ml_impurity_from_counts: entropy and Gini are checked by scikit-learn's decision-tree impurity of a node with these counts; the misclassification error by a numpy re-derivation
weak_references.ml_linear_svm_decision: decision values and classes by scikit-learn's LinearSVC with the given coefficients; the margin width and distances by numpy's norm of the same weights
weak_references.ml_logistic_regression_fit: checked against scikit-learn's fit polished by scipy's root finder on the stationarity equations (a different algorithm for the same optimum)
weak_references.ml_mean_reciprocal_rank: checked by a numpy re-derivation of the same definition (first relevant position by argmax)
weak_references.ml_perceptron_epoch: the weights and bias are checked by scikit-learn's Perceptron (one epoch, no shuffling); the update count by the shipped simulation only (no library reports it)
weak_references.ml_precision_recall_at_k: checked by a numpy re-count of the same definitions (no library computes precision@k of a ranked list)
